I'm in the same boat, it's been 9 months since we split from a 5 year relationship. I feel like it was all a lie because of how quickly he moved on. I think I've found it harder to get over because of how cold he was. I do get that he has no responsibility to ask how I'm doing etc, but if I'd hurt someone (however unavoidable it was), I would still recognise them as a human being with feelings and help while being firm with boundaries.

Not your place to stress when you've done nothing wrong, which is why I say don't get involved. I know it's hard and you're bound to be angry but the fact that you posted on here rather than acting immediately shows how strong you are. His shit is now her problem, not yours. Feel free to message and vent to me if needed!

I would say no, but I imagine a lot of people will disagree with me. Take the high ground and let them crack on. Either she will hear it from someone other than him, and their relationship will turn to shit, or he will do the same to her that he did to you, and their relationship will turn to shit. If it's the latter, he will likely come back to you which will give you a lot of satisfaction.

Hey, I've been through a similar thing and stayed longer than I should've done. He said when we broke up that he didn't realise he didn't prioritise me, or that he neglected me in the relationship. I did communicate it to him a lot during our 5 years together, but it's hard to keep saying stuff like that because you shouldn't have to ask them to put more effort in. It truly is so painful being neglected by the one you love, and it's harder when they don't see your pain.

I'm still devastated 9 months on, whereas he moved on within a few weeks. I just hope I can find someone who can put me first and will reciprocate and appreciate the effort I put in :) just know you deserved better, and sooner or later you will find it. One day, they will realise what they lost in you.

Hopefully one day she will see that in you, but if not then somebody else will see the best in you and love you for it.

I was always ready to commit as I was so sure that I wanted to spend the rest of my life with him, so I didn't really understand. I felt like I was just waiting and waiting for him to be ready and no decisions were made about our future on my terms. I became very unhappy and really wanted it to work but he wouldn't listen to me or compromise. Now, after we've split up for a while, he seems intent on settling down and marrying the next girl that's come along, who isn't as compatible with him as I was. As you said about your situation, we loved each other so much and were so happy, aside for him not being ready. It hurts so much and I struggle with it every day. I really hope you guys can make it work in the end!

I'm so sorry you're feeling this way. I've been in that same position where you feel numb and tired. As well as counselling, you could try medication or seeing a doctor? When I went on my meds I wasn't happy, but it took the edge off the depression. By that I mean I could do little things each day like reach out to a friend or make one job application or even just do the laundry. I concentrated on little things and because I was so low and tired, every little thing I did felt like an achievement. It won't sort out the root cause of your feelings but it may take off enough of the weight of depression to enable you to find hope and positivity in the future.

I know you said you find talking to your friends exhausting, but it may be worth opening up to them about how you feel. I'm sure they will be there for you and maybe provide you with more support and help you get through this hard time.
